This is scientific research, not a publication, hardware demonstration, historical-priority claim, or confirmation of Capital integration.

## What changed

- **Periodic Toda:** `toda_relative_arithmetic_root_20261029/END_TO_END_THEOREM_CANDIDATE.md` and `latent_integrable_geometry/audit/relative_interface_20261029/` assemble and review a repaired mathematical polynomial-bit construction for explicitly supplied rational positive periodic Toda data, rational time and requested original-state accuracy, including closed gaps. The verdict depends on its stated spectral/root-isolation imports and the outer-matching, inexact-domain and representation-reset repairs. It is not an arbitrary-equation discovery theorem. Equally informed conventional inverse-spectral methods can use the construction; no algorithmic superiority is established. Archival consolidation and certified arbitrary-genus software remain distinct obligations.
- **Toda diagnostics and useful failures:** full physical reconstruction, direct-ODE comparisons, rounded section arithmetic and deliberately difficult matching cases are saved with code and outputs. They are numerical diagnostics, not certified interval implementations or physical measurements. Low-precision phase agreement can coexist with failed matching admission. Existing rank-one/Jordan and conventional comparator material is retained as unchanged context.
- **Interaction-assisted discovery:** exact controlled quotient counterexamples and finite boundary/contact diagnostics show both additional information and residual blindness. The receipt covers its named exact files, not generic scalable inversion, apparatus, or novelty. Differential-mobility qualifications do not confer a free independently adjustable hidden clock. The broad discovery proposal remains rejected at the stated interface.
- **Other rejected openings:** broadcast mechanical matter and computational intervention retain concrete command/acquisition cost obstructions and strong ordinary comparators. A compact predictor does not automatically acquire interventions; serial addressing is not defeated by hiding information in an analog command. Source extracts and scientific failure records remain available.
- **Autonomous clocks and noise:** the packet develops guarded-channel intertwiners, local progress, high-reset coefficient methods, extensive no-emission estimates and chronological site/slab record bounds. The independent extensive-no-emission audit is scoped to the specified ideal Markovian clock and its stated chronological grid; poor constants and hardware realization are not removed. Two-site lease and recovery-cell constructions must be read with their own current review status, locality convention and fault limitations.
- **New graph-state factory proposal, pending review:** `GRAPH_STATE_DATA_BRIDGE.md` and its exact finite regression test whole-space dressing, combined controller/data flags and no-creation identities for the bounded-range many-body guarded model. The proposed finite-time healing argument explicitly replaces an invalid classical-sector treatment with gentle projection. The proposed arbitrary-finite-time-to-local-polynomial extension is now written but remains unreceived, as does its proposed noisy-factory consequence. No noisy-factory theorem is accepted here. `LOCAL_REPAIR_TO_SPARSE_DEFECTS.md` is a general sufficient-interface lemma, not proof that any lease or graph-state implementation satisfies its hypotheses. The many-body guarded, two-site lease and graph-state interfaces must not be combined into one proved scalable architecture. The proposed factory controls dressed-subsystem syndrome defects, not global fidelity; finite-depth decoding or dressed readout and its errors must still be charged.
- **Clock-to-data boundary:** `clock_data_fault_bridge_20261029/` distinguishes a physical-time inclusive fault-insertion bound from the failed update-index interval-noise transfer. The reset-erasure correction is essential: discarded-output resets may erase damage, so the failed completed-channel example is not evidence of faulty reduced-data output; the operational measurement-output counterexample is separately scoped. Controller liveness or equal-time defect sparsity does not establish a noisy data-computation threshold. The guarded-clock audit directory contains the independent finite replay artifacts available at this cutoff. Unless a completed scoped review is explicitly present, those tests are not a received general controller or graph-state theorem.

# Extensive joint no-emission theorem via finite-support Lyapunov polynomials

**Status: constructive proof.** This establishes an extensive joint absence bound, not merely marginal mixing. It works for arbitrary positive g,kappa and arbitrary initial full-qubit states. Constants are catastrophically weak and do not establish the sharp weak-drive scaling c(D)g^2/kappa.

Model: full qubits, H=sum_z g X_z product_{y~z}(I-n_y), jumps sqrt(kappa)sigma^-_z, graph degree <=D. Let J_x^*(A)=kappa sigma_x^+ A sigma_x^-. For a marked set S define K_S=L^*-sum_{x in S}J_x^*. Then exp(tK_S)I is the effect of no emissions anywhere in S during [0,t]. These semigroups are completely positive and subunital.

## 1. Input: uniform local progress

The local-observability theorem gives, for every delta>0, a constant c=c(D,g,kappa,delta)>0 such that

 exp(delta K_{x})I <= (1-c)I

on every graph and for every x. The earlier proof was phrased on the independent-set subspace. IMPORTANT: to apply the product construction on the full tensor product, use its full-qubit extension: the same curvature estimate holds with a larger harmless constant, because Q L*²(n_x)Q=2g²G_xQ and the self-curvature on full qubits is 2g²G_x(1-2n_x). Its difference from 2g²G_x is bounded by 4g² n_x. Neighbor-count dissipative identities and all off-diagonal bounds are unchanged. Thus the same stated curvature constant and cutoff bound work on the full-qubit model too. No illegal-configuration loophole is present.

## 2. Finite local Taylor estimates

Put

 C0=4(g+kappa)(D+2)^2,
 delta=1/(4C0), q=C0 delta=1/4,
 a=(1-exp(-kappa delta))/kappa.

For K=K_{x}, locality and nested-generator counting give

 ||K^k I|| <= C0^k k!.

Proof: artificially include x in the support from the start. A nonzero Hamiltonian/dissipator term meets current support, and K has one additional local killing term at x. At most (D+3)|support| terms matter, each norm <=2(g+kappa), and support after j terms has size <=1+jD. The displayed C0 dominates the resulting product bound. Support radius grows at most two per term. The estimate is uniform in graph size.

Define the Hermitian finite-support polynomial

 F_x^(m)=sum_{k=0}^m delta^(k+1)/(k+1)! K_x^k(I).

It is supported in B_{2m}(x). Let F_x=integral_0^delta exp(sK_x)I ds. Bounded target intensity gives exp(sK_x)I>=exp(-kappa s)I, so

 aI <= F_x <= delta I.

The series bounds give

 ||F_x^(m)-F_x|| <= delta q^(m+1)/(1-q),
 ||K_x F_x^(m) - [exp(delta K_x)I-I]|| <= q^(m+2)/(1-q).

The second estimate follows EXACTLY by applying K to the polynomial and shifting its index; no extensive global generator norm is used.

Choose an integer m such that the first error <=a/2 and second error <=c/2. This choice depends only on D,g,kappa. Then

 (a/2)I <= F_x^(m) <= (3delta/2)I,
 K_x F_x^(m) <= -(c/2)I <= -r F_x^(m),
 r=c/(3delta)>0.

## 3. Buffered packing and product inequality

Given S, greedily choose S' subset S with pairwise center distances >4m+2. A degree bound gives

 |S'| >= |S|/B,
 B=(D+1)^(4m+3)

(a deliberately loose ball-volume bound). Write s=|S'| and F=product_{x in S'} F_x^(m). These positive factors have disjoint supports. The support of L^*(F_x^(m)) lies in B_{2m+2}(x), disjoint from every other factor's support by the chosen buffer.

The Hamiltonian obeys Leibniz, and each single-site dissipator acts on at most one factor. Therefore

 [L^*-sum_{x in S'}J_x^*]F
 =sum_{x in S'} [K_x F_x^(m)] product_{z!=x}F_z^(m)
 <= -rs F.

The ordering is valid because each local negative summand commutes with the remaining positive factors on disjoint supports. Additional killings x in S\S' subtract J_x^*(F)>=0, hence

 K_S F <= -rs F.

Positivity of the killed semigroup gives exp(tK_S)F<=exp(-rst)F. Using the bounds on F yields, for EVERY initial density matrix rho,

 P_rho[N_x(t)=0 for all x in S]
 <= (3delta/a)^s exp(-rst)
 <= C^|S| exp(-gamma |S| t),

 C=3delta/a,
 gamma=r/B=c/[3delta (D+1)^(4m+3)]>0.

The probability is also <=1, so take the minimum with one. Constants are independent of graph size, S, and rho.

## 4. Actual joint spacetime consequence

For nonoverlapping chronological time slabs j, with marked site sets S_j and durations T_j, the arbitrary-initial-state bound composes under conditioning on all preceding no-event records:

 P[every (x,j) with x in S_j has no event during slab j]
 <= product_j C^|S_j| exp[-gamma |S_j|T_j].

For a fixed slab length T this is a genuine local-stochastic upper bound p^(sum_j |S_j|), where p=C exp(-gamma T), whenever p<1. No independence assumption or multiplication of marginal bounds is used: each whole-slab marked-set event has its own extensive estimate.

## 5. What remains

This is a mathematically useful existence-level joint clock-stall law. Its rate gamma can be far smaller than g^2/kappa; obtaining gamma>=c(D)g^2/kappa with moderate C(D) remains open here. Also this theorem concerns the ideal clock only, not fault propagation under physical perturbations or a complete error-correction threshold.

# Independent audit of the extensive no-emission theorem

Auditor: joint-record-bound child worker, 2026-10-29.

## Verdict

No mathematical error found. The construction does establish an existence-level extensive same-slab absence estimate, and therefore a local-stochastic bound for arbitrary marked site/slab subsets on a chronological slab grid. It does not rely on an unjustified product of marginal probabilities or on mixing alone.

## Checked steps

### Full-qubit local-progress extension

On the full qubit space, the Hamiltonian off-diagonal observable in L*n_x is O_x=ig G_x(sigma-_x-sigma+_x), not the unguarded lowering operator. Its norm is at most g. The self-site double commutator is exactly 2g^2 G_x(1-2n_x). Subtracting 2g^2 G_x leaves a diagonal term whose expectation has magnitude at most 4g^2<f>. Neighboring Hamiltonian contributions remain x-off-diagonal, with each norm <=2g^2; all non-neighbor centers commute. Dissipators outside the closed star cancel, and the remaining dissipators preserve x-off-diagonality. Consequently the previously supplied loose curvature constant remains valid. Neighbor-count damping identities are also unchanged on the full tensor product. Thus the local-progress input really applies to arbitrary illegal/full-qubit configurations as claimed.

### Local Taylor counting

Artificially counting x in the support ensures the added killing term is always included. At most (D+3)|support| local terms are relevant, with individual norm <=2(g+kappa), and the support size after j applications is <=1+jD. This yields the safe coefficient base 2(g+kappa)(D+3)(D+1), which is less than C0=4(g+kappa)(D+2)^2. The k! bound follows. No global generator norm is hidden here.

The graph radius can grow by at most two per generator application because each guarded Hamiltonian is a star, whose diameter is two. Therefore F_x^(m) is indeed supported in B_{2m}(x).

### Polynomial and shifted residual

Applying K to F_m yields sum_{j=1}^{m+1}delta^j K^j(I)/j! EXACTLY. Thus its discrepancy from exp(delta K)I-I starts at j=m+2, not m+1. The geometric tail stated in the theorem is valid.

The survival operator lower bound exp(sK)I>=exp(-kappa s)I follows from a bounded target intensity, or directly from the differential trace inequality for the unnormalized no-target state. Hence aI<=F<=delta I. Approximation error <=a/2 implies a/2<=F_m<=3delta/2. The choice r=c/(3delta) correctly turns K F_m<=-(c/2)I into K F_m<=-rF_m.

### Exact product calculation

For selected centers separated by more than 4m+2, the support B_{2m+2}(x) of L*(F_x^(m)) is disjoint from B_{2m}(z) for every other selected center z. Hamiltonian commutators satisfy the Leibniz rule exactly. Each on-site damping term acts nontrivially on at most one factor, so its dissipative product correction vanishes. Each selected J_x acts only in its own factor. Thus the displayed product-generator identity is exact.

Each operator inequality K_x F_x^(m)<=-rF_x^(m) can be multiplied by the remaining positive factors because their supports commute with the entire local summand. The sum is therefore bounded by -rs F. For additional marked sites, J_x(F)>=0 follows from complete positivity and F>=0; no support or commutation condition is needed for this subtraction.

### Semigroup comparison and extensive exponent

For a positive semigroup, K_S F<=-rsF implies exp(tK_S)F<=exp(-rst)F by applying positivity to the Duhamel integral for K_S+rs. The lower and upper scalar bounds on the product F then give (3delta/a)^s exp(-rst).

The packing bound s>=|S|/B and s<=|S| imply

 (3delta/a)^s exp(-rst)
 <=(3delta/a)^|S| exp[-(r/B)|S|t],

because 3delta/a>=3>1. The degree-dependent ball-volume overestimate B=(D+1)^(4m+3) is safe, including D=0.

### Chronological slab conditioning

After conditioning on no-target emissions in all preceding slabs, the normalized current clock state is arbitrary. The extensive one-slab theorem applies to that state, so multiplying its conditional bounds is valid. This is not conditioning on simultaneous future records. Taking T large enough that C exp(-gamma T)<1 produces the stated product over marked site/slab cells.

## Scope cautions, not proof defects

- The theorem's constants can be extremely poor; no weak-drive-optimal gamma scaling follows.
- It treats the specified ideal Markovian clock. Physical error propagation, complementary auxiliary sectors, implementations, and a fault-tolerant computational threshold remain separate issues.
- The slab law is immediate on a common chronological grid. More general overlapping time windows require a reduction or separate argument and should not be silently included.
- An empty marked set has probability one, consistent with the exponent convention.

# A rigorous physical-time inclusive fault-insertion contract

2026-10-29. This is a constructive retained-bath / nonunitary-noise contract for the **actual physical evolution**, with its completed-reset record retained. It is not yet a proof that an autonomous quantum code corrects the resulting faults. The missing conversion is identified exactly below.

## Model and locations

Work on the actual data+controller+bath Hilbert space, not an effective eliminated generator. Let L_0(t) be the clean guarded-channel generator plus arbitrary bath-only evolution. The noise is

    N(t)=sum_e [-i h_e(t), .] + sum_a D[M_a(t)].

Every h_e is bounded, with bounded system support but possibly a common retained bath. Every M_a has bounded system support and is bounded. Allow time dependence and arbitrary system-bath initial correlations. Infinite-dimensional baths require existence of the joint propagators; use an interaction picture or finite approximants for unbounded bath-only dynamics. No bath reset is used.

Partition physical time into deterministic slabs of length T. Partition the local noise terms among fixed spatial anchors, with each anchor's terms supported in a fixed-radius system neighborhood. A physical-time fault location j=(anchor, slab) denotes its assigned noise generator N_j(t), zero outside that slab. Assign each term exactly once, rather than counting one insertion as multiple locations. Define

    epsilon_j=integral ||N_j(t)||_diamond dt
              <= integral [2 sum_e ||h_e(t)|| +2 sum_a ||M_a(t)||^2] dt.

The diamond norm is on the full augmented system-bath map (and arbitrary reference), not a reduced-system Markov approximation. Assume epsilon_j<=eta T. The clean generator need not be small, have a spectral gap, mix, or be independent among clocks.

Crucial physical condition: multiplying any selected N_j by any number z_j in [0,1], while keeping all other terms fixed, leaves a legitimate CPTP generator. This holds for the Hamiltonian and added-Lindblad model above. It need not hold for arbitrary signed differences of calibrated generators; the root defect theorem's broader perturbation class is not silently inherited.

## Inclusive fault map and theorem

For a finite selected set S of physical-time locations, let E(z_S) be the full physical propagator over the experiment, with all unselected noise present at full strength and selected N_j multiplied by z_j. Define

    F(S)=sum_{A subset S} (-1)^(|S|-|A|) E(1_A).

Then

    ||F(S)||_diamond <= product_{j in S} epsilon_j <= (eta T)^|S|.    (2)

In a formal Dyson expansion around L_0, F(S) is exactly the sum of paths having at least one noise insertion from every specified location in S, with arbitrarily many additional insertions anywhere. Thus (2) is the standard *inclusive* coherent fault-path currency, not a claim that fault paths are probabilities or independent. It is uniform in total volume and runtime outside the selected locations.

### Proof

The multivariate fundamental theorem of calculus gives

    F(S)=integral_[0,1]^|S| (product_j partial_zj) E(z) dz.

Duhamel's formula expresses the mixed derivative as a sum over all temporal orderings of |S| inserted maps N_j(t_j), with the interpolated full propagator between consecutive insertions. Every intervening propagator is CPTP and has diamond norm one, because all z are in [0,1]. Apply submultiplicativity to each integrand. The time-ordering simplices, summed over permutations, partition the product integration domain (coincident-time boundaries have measure zero). Therefore the bound is precisely

    integral product_j ||N_j(t_j)||_diamond dt_j
      = product_j epsilon_j.

No factor growing with total number of unmarked locations appears. Summing the absolute values of the entire Dyson expansion instead would introduce such a factor and lose the threshold-compatible bound. The CPTP interpolation is what avoids that mistake.

## Completed channels and their real order are retained

The same theorem applies to the joint output consisting of physical quantum state plus the full classical **downward-reset time/location record**, with Kraus labels either retained or summed. This follows by taking the ordinary quantum-jump instrument of the fixed clean downward resets and adding a classical record register. For every z, the summed record instrument is CPTP. The Duhamel argument inserts N_j on the physical state while preserving already-produced records; its norm bound is unchanged. Finite time bins followed by refinement give the continuous record version.

Consequently the contract does not replace the actual correlated clock history by iid clocks, average progress, or a nominal synchronous gate order. On the zero-noise clean invariant sector, the root intertwiner says the recorded channels implement their exact completed-channel order. After insertions, the physical state and the actual records remain the objects bounded by (2), even if the state leaves that sector. Trace out the bath only at the end if desired; contractivity preserves (2).

Restricting to a particular event in the classical record is a trace-nonincreasing CP postprocessing and cannot increase the bound. **Renormalizing by that event's probability can increase the bound arbitrarily.** Thus (2) is not a uniform conditional-noise theorem for each realized clock schedule.

## What this establishes, and the single remaining semantic obstruction

Equation (2) already accommodates bounded local Hamiltonian noise with a retained, common bath and bounded local nonunitary noise. It supplies the honest physical-time fault-insertion representation the controller results were missing. A bounded-depth physical-to-abstract frame preserves bounded support up to a constant radius, and preserves Hamiltonian operator norms.

However, a physical-time insertion is not automatically a single faulty **completed data channel**. It can leave a corrupted controller whose later resets enact wrong channels, while eligibility delays can allow extensive storage damage. The interval counterexample in DATA_EXPOSURE_COUNTEREXAMPLE.md proves that discarding physical-time extent and charging only successful-update indices is unsound even for independent Poisson clocks.

To invoke a standard circuit/exRec theorem one still needs a deterministic correctness statement: for every physical fault cluster satisfying a stated geometry (and every allowed clock record), all data outside a bounded, charged neighborhood follow the intended fault-tolerant channel circuit, including entry/exit of corrupted controller sectors. Or one must prove an autonomous decoder threshold directly for (2) plus the actual clock instrument. Neither statement is obtained from equal-time B flags, single-clock liveness, or the joint no-emission bound. In particular, the record instrument itself may correlate an unmarked data update with a remote marked clock fault through a long eligibility dependency cone.

This is a precise partial bridge, not a claimed quantum-memory threshold. It isolates the unresolved task as fault **semantics and correction**, rather than the existence of a retained-bath, nonunitary physical-time fault expansion.

## Standard comparison

The norm-and-Duhamel mechanism is conventional, not claimed novel: compare Terhal–Burkard, https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0402104, and Aliferis–Gottesman–Preskill, https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0504218. Its useful specialization here is to the full guarded-clock CPTP dynamics and its completed-reset record, without eliminating controllers or resetting the environment.

# A data-exposure counterexample to update-index noise transfer

2026-10-29. Scope: rigorous counterexample for the **independent-Poisson marching-soldier scheduler**, which is the continuous-time comparator in arXiv:2601.20818. It is NOT a theorem that the guarded finite-kappa clocks have the same law, NOT a failure theorem for the particular concatenated code in that paper, and NOT a no-go for physical-time fault-cluster thresholds.

## Primary comparators checked first

Terhal–Burkard, https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0402104, and Aliferis–Gottesman–Preskill, https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0504218, establish conventional retained-bath threshold frameworks. Their relevant currency is a joint norm bound on specified faulty locations, not independence or marginal mean waiting times. The independent-Poisson construction and its claimed mean-speed-to-local-fault conversion are in https://arxiv.org/html/2601.20818v1, IV.2, especially the paragraphs following its noise model. That paper explicitly leaves general nonunitary Lindbladian noise open. The p-bounded contract in https://arxiv.org/html/2412.19803v2, Definition 3.11, quantifies over **every finite specified set**, so the set below is an admissible test.

## Scheduler and exact dependency coordinates

On a d-dimensional cubic lattice, d>=2, initially all successful-update counters are zero. A vertex can perform its next update only when its count is no larger than every neighbor's count. Independent rate-one Poisson attempts give the exact deferred-clock representation

    T(v,k)=max_{u in N[v]} T(u,k-1)+E(v,k),
    T(v,0)=0,  E(v,k) iid Exp(1).

Let z=|N[v]|=2d+1 and fix an origin o. Set s>0,

    R=floor(s/[8 log(2z)]),
    V_R={v: 1<=dist(v,o)<=R},  r=|V_R|=Theta(R^d),
    k_v=dist(v,o).

The fixed selected UPDATE locations are the intervals preceding update (v,k_v+1), for v in V_R. These are specified in advance; they are not adaptively selected from a trajectory.

Define A={E(o,1)>s}, of probability e^{-s}. The dependency path from (o,1) to (v,k_v+1) gives

    A implies T(v,k_v+1)>s  for all v in V_R.

Conversely, T(v,k_v) does not depend on E(o,1): a directed dependency path of k_v vertices can traverse at most k_v-1 graph edges. Therefore the event

    B={T(v,k_v)<=s/2 for every v in V_R}

is independent of A. Expanding the recurrence into at most z^{k_v-1} paths and using E exp(E/2)=2 gives

    Pr[T(v,k_v)>s/2] <= (2z)^{k_v} exp(-s/4) <= exp(-s/8).

Thus Pr(B)>=1-r exp(-s/8). On A intersect B, **every selected interval contains the entire physical-time interval [s/2,s]**. All selected sites are idle throughout that interval. This is the crucial joint exposure, absent from a mean-progress calculation.

## Actual bounded local nonunitary data damage

At each vertex put a data qubit. Its successful update resets it to |0>; this is a perfectly valid one-site CPTP update, with the usual neighboring counter eligibility test. Updates of other vertices do not touch this data qubit. Between updates apply independent local noise with Lindblad operator

    L_v=sqrt(lambda) |1><0|_v.

This is genuine nonunitary noise, with local generator diamond norm <=2 lambda, and is a subcase of bounded local noise with an arbitrary retained bath (take an inert bath). Given its most recent reset at t_v, the qubit is in state

    exp[-lambda(s-t_v)] |0><0| + (1-exp[-lambda(s-t_v)]) |1><1|.

On A intersect B, every t_v=T(v,k_v)<=s/2 and no further reset occurs before s. Conditional on the scheduler, the noises and output Z measurements are independent. Hence the physically observable event that **all r selected data qubits are wrong at time s** has probability at least

    exp(-s) [1-r exp(-s/8)] [1-exp(-lambda s/2)]^r.             (1)

Each wrong output witnesses a data fault in its specified interval preceding update (v,k_v+1). There is no ambiguity from a controller flag or a mere absence of updates: these are actual incorrect data values. Noise does not touch the counters.

Take s=a/lambda for any fixed a>0. If the induced update-index data-fault process were q(lambda)-bounded, (1) would force

    q(lambda) >= [1-exp(-a/2)] exp(-s/r)
                 [1-r exp(-s/8)]^(1/r).

For d>=2, r=Theta(s^d), so s/r ->0. Therefore

    liminf_{lambda->0} q(lambda) >= 1-exp(-a/2).

Since a can be any fixed positive constant, **no q(lambda)->0 interval-exposure contract exists; in fact any uniform all-times/all-volumes local-stochastic parameter for those exposures must be q>=1**. The same construction with independent unitary X Poisson noise yields a lower limiting bound approaching 1/2 through odd-jump parity; it already defeats a parameter tending to zero within the comparator's narrower noise class.

The reset-to-zero example is intentionally a minimal channel instance, not a proposed quantum code. It disproves a generic schedule-to-update-index fault-law transfer. It does not imply that a specific code cannot tolerate these extended, very rare exposure cones through a different geometric cluster argument.

## Retained coherent bath version of the interval fault obstruction

Instead of the Lindblad noise, take H_SB=h sum_v X_v tensor Z_B, with one common retained bath qubit, initially in a Z_B eigenstate. Every interaction term has norm h and one-site system support. On a long idle interval the local data undergoes a rotation of angle h times its physical duration; its channel deviation is not O(h) uniformly over the selected successful-update intervals. This provides a bounded retained-bath exposure witness, but (1) is the stronger fully quantified joint data counterexample. No assumption that a common bath generates independent faults is made or needed.

## Consequence for the root guarded-channel architecture

The root exact-channel and controller results do not justify replacing physical-time exposure by one small fault parameter per successful correction update. The root no-emission theorem concerns recorded **attempted CPTP channels**; for a marching-soldier channel a completed attempt may only test eligibility and do nothing. It does not bound the waiting time between successful counter increments. A region can receive abundant recorded resets while its data correction is stalled by a distant dependency bottleneck.

The guarded finite-kappa clocks are correlated, so the iid E representation above must NOT be imported into them. The rigorous conclusion is a decisive failure of the proposed generic transfer already for the simpler primary comparator. To finish the guarded-clock architecture one must retain physical-time cells / dependency cones and prove the chosen code corrects that fault model, or change the scheduler to bound such exposure. This document does not claim that either task has been completed.

## Operational caveat and explicit completed-instrument variant (root audit)

A reset can erase all earlier data damage. Therefore the preceding proof must **not** be quoted as saying that the subsequent reduced-data reset channel is faulty: reset-to-zero composed with any trace-preserving pre-noise is still reset-to-zero. The bound refutes a local-stochastic law for actual **interval noise exposures / pre-update data faults**, and establishes simultaneous physical data readout damage at time s. It is not by itself a witness against every possible equivalent fault representation after erasing updates.

There is an explicit way to retain the witness if the claimed contract includes the completed channel's measurement output. Implement each successful update as the ordinary two-outcome instrument

    K_0=|0><0|, K_1=|0><1|,

and retain its classical outcome along with its location and update index. It measures the incoming data bit and then resets it. In the exact guarded-Kraus compiler these are precisely the two downward-reset Kraus labels, so the result can be carried by the actual emitted reset record; it is not inferred from an occupancy flag. Equivalently supply a fresh initialized output bit for each update, copy the computational-basis value to it, then reset the data. That latter realization explicitly consumes one fresh output bit per recorded update and needs its physical output/storage interface; it is not free fixed-space hardware.

Because amplitude-raising noise leaves |1> invariant, on the wrong-data event at s each site's first later successful update (v,k_v+1) emits outcome 1. The clean instrument emits outcome 0 at every update. Therefore exactly the same lower bound (1) applies to a joint set of **observable faulty completed measurement outputs**, even though the post-reset data are clean. For the usual CPTP map that discards those outcomes, only the earlier interval-exposure statement is claimed. A threshold theorem may legitimately exploit such erasure; the counterexample is not a proof against that theorem.

The Poisson-X variant is safest stated as a joint bound on the independent noise **increments during the disjoint per-site intervals**, not the cumulative already-corrupted data. For operational output errors use the monotone nonunitary amplitude-raising construction above; it avoids cancellation before the eventual recorded update.

assessment: The actual returned source separates ideal controller progress from data protection. Its reset-erasure correction invalidates completed-channel mismatch as proof of reduced-data damage; operational measurement-output failure remains a distinct objective. No noisy-data threshold, physical fault model or graph-state factory is supplied by the liveness theorem. This is source inspection, not a new proof audit.
